cards.title: Mishnah Sanhedrin 4:5 After Cain and Abel: Saving or Killing One Soul
cards.note: Surah 5:32 moves directly from Cain killing Abel in 5:27–31 to a decree for the Sons of Israel that killing one person is like killing all mankind and saving one is like saving all mankind, matching the rabbinic homily on Genesis 4:10 in Mishnah Sanhedrin 4:5.

discussion.view: Classical commentators such as al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir explain that God revealed this legal principle to the Children of Israel in their ancient scriptures following the first human murder.
discussion.reply: In the Hebrew Bible, Genesis 4:10 records the narrative of Cain and Abel without any decree equating one life to all mankind. That maxim originates in Mishnah Sanhedrin 4:5 (c. AD 200), where rabbinic sages explicitly derive it as human courtroom commentary on the plural Hebrew word for bloods (demei) in Genesis 4:10.

cards.quranEn: From that time We prescribed for the Sons of Israel that whoever kills a person, except (in retaliation) for another, or (for) fomenting corruption on the earth, (it is) as if he had killed all the people. And whoever gives (a person) life, (it is) as if he had given all the people life. Certainly Our messengers have brought them the clear signs, yet even after that many of them act wantonly on the earth.
quranHighlights: whoever kills a person, except (in retaliation) for another, or (for) fomenting corruption on the earth, (it is) as if he had killed all the people
whoever gives (a person) life, (it is) as if he had given all the people life

sources.title: Mishnah Sanhedrin
sources.en: Therefore, Adam the first man was created alone, to teach you that with regard to anyone who destroys one soul from the Jewish people, i.e., kills one Jew, the verse ascribes him blame as if he destroyed an entire world, as Adam was one person, from whom the population of an entire world came forth. And conversely, anyone who sustains one soul from the Jewish people, the verse ascribes him credit as if he sustained an entire world.

cards.title: Pharaoh Ordering Haman to Bake Clay Bricks and Build a Tower to Heaven
cards.note: Surah 28:38–42 portrays Pharaoh in Egypt ordering Haman to bake clay bricks and build a lofty tower to climb to the God of Moses, combining the baked-brick tower of Babel (Genesis 11:3–4; Sanhedrin 109a) with Haman from the Persian court of Esther 3:1.

discussion.view: Muslim commentators and modern harmonizers propose that Haman was either an unrecorded Egyptian court minister or a title of an Egyptian quarry official distinct from the Persian vizier in the Book of Esther.
discussion.reply: In the Hebrew Bible, Haman the Agagite serves King Ahasuerus (Xerxes) in fifth-century BC Persia (Esther 3:1), roughly a millennium after Moses and Pharaoh in New Kingdom Egypt. Furthermore, firing clay bricks in a kiln to build a tower reaching the heavens is the specific architectural motif of Mesopotamia's Tower of Babel in Genesis 11:3–4 rather than Egyptian stone masonry.

cards.quranEn: [38] Pharaoh said, ‘Assembly! I know of no other god for you than me. So light a fire for me, Haman, on the clay, and make a tower for me, so that I may look at the god of Moses. Surely I think he is indeed one of the liars.’ [39] He and his forces became arrogant on the earth without any right, and thought that they would not be returned to Us. [40] So We seized him and his forces, and tossed them into the sea. See how the end was for the evildoers! [41] We made them leaders (who) call (others) to the Fire, and on the Day of Resurrection they will not be helped. [42] We pursued them in this world with a curse, and on the Day of Resurrection they will be among the scorned.

cards.title: Abraham Breaking All the Idols Except the Largest One in Bereishit Rabbah
cards.note: Surah 21:51–67 narrates Abraham breaking his people's idols into pieces except the largest statue and telling his accusers that the largest idol did it and they should ask the statues if they can speak, matching Bereishit Rabbah 38:13.

discussion.view: Traditional commentators hold that the Quran restores the historical account of young Abraham's confrontation with his father's idolatrous community in Mesopotamia.
discussion.reply: Genesis 11:28–31 states that Terah and Abram departed from Ur of the Chaldees (`Ur Kasdim`). Because the Hebrew noun `ur` also means fire, Second Temple and rabbinic exegetes (Jubilees 12; Bereishit Rabbah 38:13) crafted a midrashic story in which Abraham breaks his father's idols, blames the largest statue, and is cast into Nimrod's furnace (`ur`).

cards.quranEn: [51] Certainly We gave Abraham his right (path) before (them), (for) We knew him. [52] (Remember) when he said to his father and his people: ‘What are these images which you are devoted to?’ [53] They said, ‘We found our fathers serving them.’ [54] He said, ‘Certainly you and your fathers were clearly astray.’ [55] They said, ‘Have you brought us the truth, or are you one of those who jest?’ [56] He said, ‘No! Your Lord – Lord of the heavens and the earth – is the One who created them, and I am one of the witnesses to this. [57] By God! I shall indeed plot (to destroy) your idols after you have turned away, withdrawing.’ [58] So he broke them into pieces, (all) except a big one they had, so that they would return to it. [59] They said, ‘Who has done this with our gods? Surely he is indeed one of the evildoers.’ [60] They said, ‘We heard a young man mentioning them – he is called Abraham.’ [61] They said, ‘Bring him before the eyes of the people, so that they may bear witness.’ [62] They said, ‘Have you done this with our gods, Abraham?’ [63] He said, ‘No! This big one of them did it. Just ask them, if they are able to speak.’ [64] And they turned to each other, and said, ‘Surely you – you are the evildoers.’ [65] Then they became utterly confused: ‘Certainly you know (that) these do not speak.’ [66] He said, ‘Do you serve what does not benefit you at all, or harm you, instead of God (alone)? [67] Uff to you and to what you serve instead of God! Will you not understand?’

sources.title: Midrash Bereishit Rabbah (Genesis Rabbah)
sources.en: One time, a certain woman came, carrying a dish of fine flour in her hand. She said to him: ‘Here, offer it before them.’ He arose, took a club in his hand, shattered all the idols, and placed the club in the hand of the largest among them. When his father came, he said to him: ‘Who did this to them?’ He said to him: ‘I will not lie to you, a certain woman came, carrying a dish of fine flour in her hand. She said to me: Here, offer it before them. I offered it before them. This one [idol] said: I shall eat first, and another one said: I shall eat first. This big idol, who was standing among them, got up and took the club and shattered them.’ He [Teraḥ] said to him: ‘What, are you mocking me? Are they sentient at all?’ He said to him: ‘Do your ears not hear what your mouth is saying?’ He [Teraḥ] took him and handed him over to Nimrod.

cards.title: The Queen of Sheba Taking Solomon's Glass Palace Floor for Deep Water
cards.note: Surah 27:38–44 culminates with the Queen of Sheba entering Solomon's palace, supposing its polished crystal floor is a pool of water, and uncovering her legs, matching the Aramaic glass-house narrative in Targum Sheni on Esther 1:2.

discussion.view: Muslim commentators such as al-Tabari and al-Qurtubi treat the crystal pavilion and the uncovering of the Queen's legs as historical events from Solomon's royal court in Jerusalem.
discussion.reply: First Kings 10:1–13 and 2 Chronicles 9:1–12 record the Queen of Sheba's visit to Solomon without any mention of a glass floor, a hoopoe messenger, or the Queen lifting her garments over water. That sequence comes from the Galilean Aramaic Targum Sheni on Esther 1:2, an aggadic expansion of Solomon's court.

cards.quranEn: [38] He said, ‘Assembly! Which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in surrender?’ [39] A crafty one of the jinn said, ‘I shall bring it to you before you (can) rise from your place. Surely I have strength for it (and am) trustworthy.’ [40] One who had knowledge of the Book said, ‘I will bring it to you in the wink of an eye.’ So when he saw it set before him, he said, ‘This is from the favor of my Lord to test me (to see) whether I am thankful or ungrateful. Whoever is thankful is thankful only for his own good, and whoever is ungrateful – surely my Lord is wealthy, generous.’ [41] He said, ‘Disguise her throne for her. We shall see whether she is (rightly) guided or is one of those who are not (rightly) guided.’ [42] So when she came, it was said, ‘Is your throne like this?’ She said, ‘It seems like it.’ ‘And we had been given the knowledge before her, and were in surrender, [43] but what she served, instead of God, kept her back. Surely she was from a disbelieving people.’ [44] It was said to her, ‘Enter the palace.’ When she saw it, she thought it was a pool (of water), and she uncovered her legs. He said, ‘Surely it is a polished palace of crystal.’ She said, ‘My Lord, surely I have done myself evil. I surrender with Solomon to God, Lord of the worlds.’

sources.title: Targum Sheni on Esther
sources.en: When King Solomon heard that she had come to him, King Solomon rose and went and sat in a house of glass. She thought in her heart that the king was sitting in water, and she lifted her skirts to cross over, and he saw that there was hair on her legs. King Solomon said, “Your beauty is the beauty of women, but your hair is the hair of a man. Hair is becoming to a man but shameful to a woman.”

cards.quranAr: قَالَ يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلۡمَلَؤُاْ أَيُّكُمۡ يَأۡتِينِي بِعَرۡشِهَا قَبۡلَ أَن يَأۡتُونِي مُسۡلِمِينَ ﴿38﴾ قَالَ عِفۡرِيتٞ مِّنَ ٱلۡجِنِّ أَنَا۠ ءَاتِيكَ بِهِۦ قَبۡلَ أَن تَقُومَ مِن مَّقَامِكَۖ وَإِنِّي عَلَيۡهِ لَقَوِيٌّ أَمِينٞ ﴿39﴾ قَالَ ٱلَّذِي عِندَهُۥ عِلۡمٞ مِّنَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ أَنَا۠ ءَاتِيكَ بِهِۦ قَبۡلَ أَن يَرۡتَدَّ إِلَيۡكَ طَرۡفُكَۚ فَلَمَّا رَءَاهُ مُسۡتَقِرًّا عِندَهُۥ قَالَ هَٰذَا مِن فَضۡلِ رَبِّي لِيَبۡلُوَنِيٓ ءَأَشۡكُرُ أَمۡ أَكۡفُرُۖ وَمَن شَكَرَ فَإِنَّمَا يَشۡكُرُ لِنَفۡسِهِۦۖ وَمَن كَفَرَ فَإِنَّ رَبِّي غَنِيّٞ كَرِيمٞ ﴿40﴾ قَالَ نَكِّرُواْ لَهَا عَرۡشَهَا نَنظُرۡ أَتَهۡتَدِيٓ أَمۡ تَكُونُ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ لَا يَهۡتَدُونَ ﴿41﴾ فَلَمَّا جَآءَتۡ قِيلَ أَهَٰكَذَا عَرۡشُكِۖ قَالَتۡ كَأَنَّهُۥ هُوَۚ وَأُوتِينَا ٱلۡعِلۡمَ مِن قَبۡلِهَا وَكُنَّا مُسۡلِمِينَ ﴿42﴾ وَصَدَّهَا مَا كَانَت تَّعۡبُدُ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِۖ إِنَّهَا كَانَتۡ مِن قَوۡمٖ كَٰفِرِينَ ﴿43﴾ قِيلَ لَهَا ٱدۡخُلِي ٱلصَّرۡحَۖ فَلَمَّا رَأَتۡهُ حَسِبَتۡهُ لُجَّةٗ وَكَشَفَتۡ عَن سَاقَيۡهَاۚ قَالَ إِنَّهُۥ صَرۡحٞ مُّمَرَّدٞ مِّن قَوَارِيرَۗ قَالَتۡ رَبِّ إِنِّي ظَلَمۡتُ نَفۡسِي وَأَسۡلَمۡتُ مَعَ سُلَيۡمَٰنَ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ ﴿44﴾

cards.title: God Suspending Mount Sinai Above Israel Like an Overhanging Canopy (Zullah)
cards.note: Surah 7:171 states that God shook Mount Sinai above the Israelites as if it were an overhanging canopy (`zullah`) so that they thought it would fall upon them, matching the Talmudic aggadah of Sinai overturned above Israel like a tub in Shabbat 88a.

discussion.view: Traditional commentators such as al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir write that angels physically uprooted Mount Sinai and held it suspended over the heads of the Israelites until they accepted the covenant.
discussion.reply: In Exodus 19:17, the Hebrew phrase `be-tachtit ha-har` means 'at the foot of the mountain,' describing Israel standing at the base of Sinai. In Talmud Bavli Shabbat 88a and Avodah Zarah 2b, third-century amora Rav Avdimi bar Hama homiletically renders `tachtit` as 'beneath' to picture the mountain held overhead like an upturned cask (`gigit`).

cards.quranEn: (Remember) when We shook the mountain above them, as if it were a canopy, and they thought it was going to fall on them: ‘Hold fast what We have given you, and remember what is in it, so that you may guard (yourselves).’
quranHighlights: We shook the mountain above them, as if it were a canopy, and they thought it was going to fall on them

sources.title: Talmud Bavli Shabbat 88a
sources.en: Rabbi Avdimi bar Ḥama bar Ḥasa said: the Jewish people actually stood beneath the mountain, and the verse teaches that the Holy One, Blessed be He, overturned the mountain above the Jews like a tub, and said to them: If you accept the Torah, excellent, and if not, there will be your burial.

cards.title: Korah (Qarun) Whose Treasure Keys Burdened a Troop of Men in Sanhedrin 110a
cards.note: Surah 28:76–82 states that Qarun (Korah) among the people of Moses possessed treasures whose keys burdened a company of strong men before the earth swallowed him, matching Talmud Bavli Sanhedrin 110a and Pesachim 119a.

discussion.view: Traditional commentators explain that God granted Qarun vast wealth among the Israelites in Egypt or the wilderness, and al-Tabari transmits reports that his leather treasury keys required dozens of mule-loads to carry.
discussion.reply: In Numbers 16:1–33, Korah leads a Levitical priesthood dispute against Moses and Aaron without any mention of vast monetary wealth or heavy treasury keys. The detail that the keys (`aklidei`) to Korah's treasuries were a load requiring three hundred white mules originates in the rabbinic aggadah of Rabbi Levi in Talmud Bavli Sanhedrin 110a and Pesachim 119a.

cards.quranEn: [76] Surely Qārūn was one of the people of Moses, and acted oppressively toward them. We had given him treasures, the keys of which would indeed have been a burden for a group (of men) endowed with strength. (Remember) when his people said to him, ‘Do not gloat! Surely God does not love those who gloat. [77] But seek the Home of the Hereafter by means of what God has given you, and do not forget your portion of this world. Do good, as God has done good to you, and do not seek to foment corruption on the earth. Surely God does not love the fomenters of corruption.’ [78] He said, ‘I have been given it only because of the knowledge (that is) in me.’ Did he not know that God had destroyed those of the generations before him who were stronger than him and had accumulated more? The sinners will not be questioned about their sins. [79] So he went forth to his people in his splendor. Those who desired this present life said, ‘Would that we had the same as what has been given to Qārūn! Surely he is indeed the possessor of great good luck.’ [80] But those to whom knowledge had been given said, ‘Woe to you! The reward of God is better for the one who believes and does righteousness. But no one will obtain it except the patient.’ [81] So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home, and he had no cohort to help him, other than God, and he was not one of those who could help themselves. [82] In the morning those who had longed (to be in) his place the day before were saying, ‘Woe (to Qārūn)! Surely God extends (His) provision to whomever He pleases of His servants, and restricts (it). If God had not bestowed favor on us, He would indeed have caused (the earth) to swallow us (too). Woe to him! The disbelievers will not prosper.’
quranHighlights: Surely Qārūn was one of the people of Moses, and acted oppressively toward them. We had given him treasures, the keys of which would indeed have been a burden for a group (of men) endowed with strength.

cards.quranAr: ۞إِنَّ قَٰرُونَ كَانَ مِن قَوۡمِ مُوسَىٰ فَبَغَىٰ عَلَيۡهِمۡۖ وَءَاتَيۡنَٰهُ مِنَ ٱلۡكُنُوزِ مَآ إِنَّ مَفَاتِحَهُۥ لَتَنُوٓأُ بِٱلۡعُصۡبَةِ أُوْلِي ٱلۡقُوَّةِ إِذۡ قَالَ لَهُۥ قَوۡمُهُۥ لَا تَفۡرَحۡۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلۡفَرِحِينَ ﴿76﴾ وَٱبۡتَغِ فِيمَآ ءَاتَىٰكَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلدَّارَ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةَۖ وَلَا تَنسَ نَصِيبَكَ مِنَ ٱلدُّنۡيَاۖ وَأَحۡسِن كَمَآ أَحۡسَنَ ٱللَّهُ إِلَيۡكَۖ وَلَا تَبۡغِ ٱلۡفَسَادَ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُفۡسِدِينَ ﴿77﴾ قَالَ إِنَّمَآ أُوتِيتُهُۥ عَلَىٰ عِلۡمٍ عِندِيٓۚ أَوَلَمۡ يَعۡلَمۡ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ قَدۡ أَهۡلَكَ مِن قَبۡلِهِۦ مِنَ ٱلۡقُرُونِ مَنۡ هُوَ أَشَدُّ مِنۡهُ قُوَّةٗ وَأَكۡثَرُ جَمۡعٗاۚ وَلَا يُسۡـَٔلُ عَن ذُنُوبِهِمُ ٱلۡمُجۡرِمُونَ ﴿78﴾ فَخَرَجَ عَلَىٰ قَوۡمِهِۦ فِي زِينَتِهِۦۖ قَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ يُرِيدُونَ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنۡيَا يَٰلَيۡتَ لَنَا مِثۡلَ مَآ أُوتِيَ قَٰرُونُ إِنَّهُۥ لَذُو حَظٍّ عَظِيمٖ ﴿79﴾ وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡعِلۡمَ وَيۡلَكُمۡ ثَوَابُ ٱللَّهِ خَيۡرٞ لِّمَنۡ ءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحٗاۚ وَلَا يُلَقَّىٰهَآ إِلَّا ٱلصَّـٰبِرُونَ ﴿80﴾ فَخَسَفۡنَا بِهِۦ وَبِدَارِهِ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ فَمَا كَانَ لَهُۥ مِن فِئَةٖ يَنصُرُونَهُۥ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ وَمَا كَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُنتَصِرِينَ ﴿81﴾ وَأَصۡبَحَ ٱلَّذِينَ تَمَنَّوۡاْ مَكَانَهُۥ بِٱلۡأَمۡسِ يَقُولُونَ وَيۡكَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَبۡسُطُ ٱلرِّزۡقَ لِمَن يَشَآءُ مِنۡ عِبَادِهِۦ وَيَقۡدِرُۖ لَوۡلَآ أَن مَّنَّ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡنَا لَخَسَفَ بِنَاۖ وَيۡكَأَنَّهُۥ لَا يُفۡلِحُ ٱلۡكَٰفِرُونَ ﴿82﴾

cards.title: Angels Objecting to Man's Creation and Unable to Name the Creatures
cards.note: Surah 2:30–33 recounts the angels questioning why God would create a human who sheds blood, being unable to name the creatures when tested, and Adam naming them all, matching Midrash Bereishit Rabbah 17:4 and Talmud Sanhedrin 38b.

discussion.view: Classical commentators explain that God informed the angels of Adam's appointment on earth and demonstrated Adam's divinely taught knowledge by having him name every creature before them.
discussion.reply: In Genesis 1:26 and 2:19–20, Adam names the animals without any angelic protest or competition. Rabbinic midrashim (Bereishit Rabbah 8:5; 17:4; Bavli Sanhedrin 38b) created this dialogue to explain why Genesis 1:26 uses the plural 'Let us make man,' portraying God consulting the ministering angels, the angels objecting to human sinfulness, and Adam surpassing them by naming the creatures.

cards.quranEn: [30] (Remember) when your Lord said to the angels, ‘Surely I am placing on the earth a ruler.’ They said, ‘Will You place on it someone who will foment corruption on it, and shed blood, while we glorify (You) with Your praise and call You holy?’ He said, ‘Surely I know what you do not know.’ [31] And He taught Adam the names – all of them. Then He presented them to the angels, and said, ‘Inform Me of the names of these, if you are truthful.’ [32] They said, ‘Glory to You! We have no knowledge except for what You have taught us. Surely You – You are the Knowing, the Wise.’ [33] He said, ‘Adam! Inform them of their names.’ And when he had informed them of their names, He said, ‘Did I not say to you, “Surely I know the unseen (things) of the heavens and the earth”? I know what you reveal and what you have concealed.’

sources.title: Genesis Rabbah 17:4
sources.en: Rabbi Aḥa said: When the Holy One blessed be He came to create man, He consulted with the ministering angels. He said to them: “Let us make man” (Genesis 1:26). They said to Him: ‘This man, what is his nature?’ He said to them: ‘His wisdom is greater than yours.’ He brought the animals, the beasts, and the birds before them and said to them: ‘What is its name of this one?’ And they did not know. He passed them before Adam and said to him: ‘What is the name of this one?’ He said: ‘This is an ox; this is a donkey; this is a horse; this is a camel.’ [He then asked:] ‘And you, what is your name?’ He said to Him: ‘It is appropriate that I be called Adam, as I was created from the ground [adama].’ [He asked further:] ‘And I, what is My name?’ He said to Him: ‘It is appropriate to call you my Lord [adonai], as You are the Lord [adon] over all your creatures.’

sources.title: Babylonian Talmud, Sanhedrin 38b
sources.en: Rav Yehuda says that Rav says: At the time that the Holy One, Blessed be He, sought to create a person, He created one group of ministering angels. He said to them: If you agree, let us fashion a person in our image. The angels said before him: Master of the Universe, what are the actions of this person You suggest to create? God said to them: His actions are such and such, according to human nature. The angels said before him: Master of the Universe: “What is man that You are mindful of him? And the son of man that You think of him?” (Psalms 8:5), i.e., a creature such as this is not worth creating. God outstretched His small finger among them and burned them with fire.

sources.en: Rabbi Simon said: When the Holy One blessed be He came to create Adam the first man, the ministering angels divided into various factions and various groups. Some of them were saying: ‘Let him not be created,’ and some of them were saying: ‘Let him be created.’ That is what is written: “Kindness and truth met; righteousness and peace touched” (Psalms 85:11). cards.title: A Raven Sent to Scratch the Earth and Show How to Bury Abel's Corpse
cards.note: Surah 5:31 describes God sending a raven scratching in the earth to show Cain how to bury his brother Abel's corpse, paralleling Midrash Bereishit Rabbah 22:8 where the birds of the heavens and clean beasts bury Abel's body.

discussion.view: Muslim commentators explain that because Abel was the first human to die on earth, Cain did not know how to dispose of a corpse until God sent a raven to dig in the soil before him.
discussion.reply: Genesis 4:8–10 makes no mention of birds or burial instructions after Cain slays Abel. In fifth-century Palestinian Midrash Bereishit Rabbah 22:8, Rabbi Elazar ben Pedat addresses how Abel was buried by stating that the birds of the heavens and kosher beasts buried him, a midrashic motif that precedes the next verse's citation of Mishnah Sanhedrin 4:5 in Surah 5:32.

cards.quranEn: Then God raised up a raven, scratching in the earth, to show him how to hide the shame of his brother. He said, ‘Woe is me! Am I unable to be like this raven, and hide the shame of my brother?’ And then he became one of the regretful.
quranHighlights: God raised up a raven, scratching in the earth, to show him how to hide the shame of his brother

sources.title: Midrash Bereishit Rabbah (Genesis Rabbah)

sources.en: Who buried him? Rabbi Elazar ben Pedat said: The birds of the heavens and the kosher beasts buried him, and the Holy One blessed be He rewarded them with the two blessings that one recites over them – one for slaughter and one for covering the blood.

cards.title: Jacob Commanding His Sons Not to Enter Egypt Through a Single Gate
cards.note: Surah 12:58–68 includes a specific command in 12:67 where Jacob tells his sons not to enter Egypt by one gate but by separate gates, matching Jacob's verbatim instruction in Midrash Bereishit Rabbah 91:2.

discussion.view: Classical commentators such as al-Tabari, al-Baghawi, and Ibn Kathir explicitly state that Jacob feared the 'evil eye' (`al-'ayn`) striking his eleven handsome sons if they entered the royal city together through a single gate.
discussion.reply: Genesis 42–43 records Jacob sending his sons to Egypt to buy grain without any instruction about city gates or the evil eye. Both the command in Surah 12:67 ('Do not enter by one gate') and the exact rationale cited by Islamic commentators ('so that the evil eye will not have dominion over you') come directly from the fifth-century rabbinic commentary Bereishit Rabbah 91:2.

cards.quranEn: [58] The brothers of Joseph came, and they entered upon him. He recognized them, but they did not know him. [59] When he had supplied them with their supplies, he said, ‘Bring me a brother of yours from your father. Do you not see that I fill up the measure, and that I am the best of hosts? [60] But if you do not bring him to me, (there will be) no measure for you with me, and you will not come near me.’ [61] They said, ‘We shall solicit his father for him. Surely we shall indeed do (so).’ [62] He said to his young men, ‘Put their merchandise (back) in their packs, so that they will recognize it when they turn back to their family, (and) so that they will return (here).’ [63] When they returned to their father, they said, ‘Our father! The measure was refused us, so send our brother (back) with us, (and) we shall get the measure. Surely we shall indeed watch over him.’ [64] He said, ‘Shall I trust you with him as I trusted you with his brother before? God is the best Watcher, and He (is) the most compassionate of the compassionate.’ [65] When they opened their belongings, they found their merchandise returned to them. They said, ‘Our father, what (more) do we desire? This is our merchandise returned to us. We shall supply (food for) our family, and watch over our brother, and get an extra measure of a camel(-load). That is an easy measure.’ [66] He said, ‘I shall not send him with you until you give me a promise from God that you will indeed bring him (back) to me, unless you are surrounded.’ When they had given him their pledge, he said, ‘God is guardian over what we say.’ [67] And he said, ‘My sons! Do not enter by one gate, but enter by different gates. I am of no use to you at all against God. Judgment (belongs) only to God. In Him have I put my trust, and in Him let the trusting put their trust.’ [68] When they had entered in the way their father commanded them – it was of no use to them at all against God, but (it was only) a need in Jacob himself which he satisfied. Surely he was indeed full of knowledge because of what We had taught him, but most of the people do not know (it).
quranHighlights: And he said, ‘My sons! Do not enter by one gate, but enter by different gates.

cards.quranAr: وَجَآءَ إِخۡوَةُ يُوسُفَ فَدَخَلُواْ عَلَيۡهِ فَعَرَفَهُمۡ وَهُمۡ لَهُۥ مُنكِرُونَ ﴿58﴾ وَلَمَّا جَهَّزَهُم بِجَهَازِهِمۡ قَالَ ٱئۡتُونِي بِأَخٖ لَّكُم مِّنۡ أَبِيكُمۡۚ أَلَا تَرَوۡنَ أَنِّيٓ أُوفِي ٱلۡكَيۡلَ وَأَنَا۠ خَيۡرُ ٱلۡمُنزِلِينَ ﴿59﴾ فَإِن لَّمۡ تَأۡتُونِي بِهِۦ فَلَا كَيۡلَ لَكُمۡ عِندِي وَلَا تَقۡرَبُونِ ﴿60﴾ قَالُواْ سَنُرَٰوِدُ عَنۡهُ أَبَاهُ وَإِنَّا لَفَٰعِلُونَ ﴿61﴾ وَقَالَ لِفِتۡيَٰنِهِ ٱجۡعَلُواْ بِضَٰعَتَهُمۡ فِي رِحَالِهِمۡ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَعۡرِفُونَهَآ إِذَا ٱنقَلَبُوٓاْ إِلَىٰٓ أَهۡلِهِمۡ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَرۡجِعُونَ ﴿62﴾ فَلَمَّا رَجَعُوٓاْ إِلَىٰٓ أَبِيهِمۡ قَالُواْ يَـٰٓأَبَانَا مُنِعَ مِنَّا ٱلۡكَيۡلُ فَأَرۡسِلۡ مَعَنَآ أَخَانَا نَكۡتَلۡ وَإِنَّا لَهُۥ لَحَٰفِظُونَ ﴿63﴾ قَالَ هَلۡ ءَامَنُكُمۡ عَلَيۡهِ إِلَّا كَمَآ أَمِنتُكُمۡ عَلَىٰٓ أَخِيهِ مِن قَبۡلُ فَٱللَّهُ خَيۡرٌ حَٰفِظٗاۖ وَهُوَ أَرۡحَمُ ٱلرَّـٰحِمِينَ ﴿64﴾ وَلَمَّا فَتَحُواْ مَتَٰعَهُمۡ وَجَدُواْ بِضَٰعَتَهُمۡ رُدَّتۡ إِلَيۡهِمۡۖ قَالُواْ يَـٰٓأَبَانَا مَا نَبۡغِيۖ هَٰذِهِۦ بِضَٰعَتُنَا رُدَّتۡ إِلَيۡنَاۖ وَنَمِيرُ أَهۡلَنَا وَنَحۡفَظُ أَخَانَا وَنَزۡدَادُ كَيۡلَ بَعِيرٖۖ ذَٰلِكَ كَيۡلٞ يَسِيرٞ ﴿65﴾ قَالَ لَنۡ أُرۡسِلَهُۥ مَعَكُمۡ حَتَّىٰ تُؤۡتُونِ مَوۡثِقٗا مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ لَتَأۡتُنَّنِي بِهِۦٓ إِلَّآ أَن يُحَاطَ بِكُمۡۖ فَلَمَّآ ءَاتَوۡهُ مَوۡثِقَهُمۡ قَالَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ مَا نَقُولُ وَكِيلٞ ﴿66﴾ وَقَالَ يَٰبَنِيَّ لَا تَدۡخُلُواْ مِنۢ بَابٖ وَٰحِدٖ وَٱدۡخُلُواْ مِنۡ أَبۡوَٰبٖ مُّتَفَرِّقَةٖۖ وَمَآ أُغۡنِي عَنكُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ مِن شَيۡءٍۖ إِنِ ٱلۡحُكۡمُ إِلَّا لِلَّهِۖ عَلَيۡهِ تَوَكَّلۡتُۖ وَعَلَيۡهِ فَلۡيَتَوَكَّلِ ٱلۡمُتَوَكِّلُونَ ﴿67﴾ وَلَمَّا دَخَلُواْ مِنۡ حَيۡثُ أَمَرَهُمۡ أَبُوهُم مَّا كَانَ يُغۡنِي عَنۡهُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ مِن شَيۡءٍ إِلَّا حَاجَةٗ فِي نَفۡسِ يَعۡقُوبَ قَضَىٰهَاۚ وَإِنَّهُۥ لَذُو عِلۡمٖ لِّمَا عَلَّمۡنَٰهُ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ ﴿68﴾

cards.title: The Man Sleeping a Hundred Years Beside His Donkey and Unspoiled Food
cards.note: Surah 2:259 recounts a traveler questioning how a ruined city will be restored, sleeping for a hundred years beside his food and his donkey while supposing a single day has passed, matching the Talmudic narrative of Honi ha-Me'aggel in Taanit 23a.

discussion.view: Commentators such as al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir identify the traveler variously as Ezra (`Uzayr`), Jeremiah, or Khidr passing by Jerusalem after its destruction by Nebuchadnezzar.
discussion.reply: In Talmud Bavli Taanit 23a, Honi ha-Me'aggel questions how the 70-year Babylonian exile of Jerusalem relates to Psalm 126:1, falls asleep beside his donkey and food for 70 years, and wakes to learn that generations have passed. Surah 2:259 fuses this Talmudic sleeper-and-donkey narrative with Ezekiel's vision of dry bones clothed with sinews and flesh in Ezekiel 37:7–8.

cards.quranEn: Or (have you not considered) the example of the one who passed by a town that had collapsed in ruins? He said, ‘How will God give this (town) life after its death?’ So God caused him to die for a hundred years, (and) then raised him up. He said, ‘How long have you remained (dead)?’ He said, ‘I have remained (dead) for a day or part of a day.’ He said, ‘No! You have remained (dead) for a hundred years. Look at your food and drink, it has not spoiled, and look at your donkey – and (this happened) so that We might make you a sign to the people – and look at the bones, how We raise them up, (and) then clothe them with flesh.’ So when it became clear to him, he said, ‘I know that God is powerful over everything.’
quranHighlights: So God caused him to die for a hundred years, (and) then raised him up.
Look at your food and drink, it has not spoiled, and look at your donkey

sources.title: Babylonian Talmud, Taanit 23a
sources.en: Ḥoni sat and ate bread. Sleep overcame him and he slept. A cliff formed around him, and he disappeared from sight and slept for seventy years. When he awoke, he saw a certain man gathering carobs from that tree. Ḥoni said to him: Are you the one who planted this tree? The man said to him: I am his son’s son. Ḥoni said to him: I can learn from this that I have slept for seventy years, and indeed he saw that his donkey had sired several herds during those many years.
highlights: Ḥoni sat and ate bread. Sleep overcame him and he slept. A cliff formed around him, and he disappeared from sight and slept for seventy years.

cards.title: Potiphar's Wife Threatening Joseph in Yoma 35b
cards.note: Surah 12:30–34 depicts Potiphar's wife demanding Joseph's submission and threatening him beforehand with imprisonment and humiliation unless he obeys her command, paralleling her explicit prison threat in Talmud Bavli Yoma 35b.

discussion.view: Traditional commentators present the banquet of the Egyptian women and the verbal threats of Potiphar's wife as revealed historical details expanding the brief account of Joseph's temptation.
discussion.reply: In Genesis 39:7–20, Potiphar's wife propositions Joseph in private and has him imprisoned after he flees, without first threatening him with prison to coerce his compliance. That explicit pre-imprisonment threat appears in fifth-century rabbinic literature in Talmud Bavli Yoma 35b, where she tells Joseph she will incarcerate him in prison and bend his stature with suffering if he refuses to submit.

cards.title: Demons in Solomon's Reign and the Two Angels Harut and Marut in Babylon
cards.note: Surah 2:102 links demons in Solomon's kingdom teaching magic with two angels in Babylon named Harut and Marut, combining 1 Enoch 7–8 on fallen angels teaching sorcery with Talmud Gittin 68a on Solomon's male and female demons.

discussion.view: Classical exegetes explain that Surah 2:102 exonerates Solomon of practicing sorcery while affirming that God sent two angels, Harut and Marut, to Babylon as a test regarding magic.
discussion.reply: The narrative combines three Near Eastern traditions: Talmudic legends in Gittin 68a giving Solomon authority over demons, the Second Temple Book of Watchers (1 Enoch 7–8) where angels descend and teach humans charms and root-cuttings, and the paired Zoroastrian archangels (`Amesha Spentas`) Haurvatat/Horvadad and Ameretat/Amerodad, whose Middle Persian names correspond philologically to Harut and Marut.

Neither of them taught anyone, unless they both (first) said, ‘We are only a temptation, so do not disbelieve.’ And they learned from both of them how to separate a husband from his wife. Yet they did not harm anyone in this way, except by the permission of God. What they learned (only) harmed them and did not benefit them. Certainly they knew that whoever buys it has no share in the Hereafter. Evil indeed is what they have sold themselves for, if (only) they knew.

cards.title: Transgressors Transformed into Apes as Divine Punishment in Sanhedrin 109a
cards.note: Surah 2:65–66 recounts God punishing Israelite Sabbath violators by commanding them, 'Become apes, skulking away,' paralleling the Talmudic punishment in Sanhedrin 109a where rebels against God are transformed into apes.

discussion.view: Traditional commentators such as al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir state that an Israelite coastal community violated the Sabbath by trapping fish on Saturday and was physically transformed into apes for three days before perishing.
discussion.reply: In the Torah (Exodus 31:14–15; Numbers 15:32–36), the penalty for Sabbath violation is capital execution, and no biblical passage records humans being transformed into apes. Physical transformation of rebels against God into apes (`kofim`) is a rabbinic aggadic punishment recorded by Rabbi Yirmeya bar Elazar in Talmud Bavli Sanhedrin 109a.

cards.title: Four Sequential Embryological Stages Clothed With Bones and Flesh
cards.note: Surah 23:12–14 describes human development from clay extract to a drop of fluid (`nutfah`), a clot (`alaqah`), a lump (`mudghah`), and bones clothed with flesh, matching the blood-and-flesh gestational stages in Talmud Bavli Niddah 25a.

discussion.view: Traditional and modern commentators present the four stages in Surah 23:12–14—drop, clot, lump, and bones clothed with flesh—as revealed scientific knowledge of human gestation.
discussion.reply: Each stage mirrors Late Antique medical and rabbinic models: Talmud Bavli Niddah 25a distinguishes early gestational sacs 'full of blood' from the subsequent stage 'full of flesh' (cf. Niddah 30b–31a), while Galen's De Semine (On Semen I.8–10, CMG V 3,1) divides embryogenesis into four sequential stages from seminal fluid to a blood-filled coagulum, an unarticulated fleshy mass, and hardened bones subsequently clothed with muscle.

So blessed (be) God, the best of creators!

cards.title: Earth Created Before the Heavens and Seven Heavens Formed from Smoke
cards.note: Surah 41:9–12 places the earth's creation and mountains before the fashioning of seven heavens from smoke, matching Beit Hillel's earth-first order in Talmud Chagigah 12a and the seven firmaments of Chagigah 12b.

discussion.view: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir harmonize the sequence in 41:9–12 with 79:27–30 by distinguishing the initial creation of the unformed earth before the seven heavens from the later spreading out (daha) of the terrestrial surface after the sky was completed.
discussion.reply: Genesis 1:1–8 places the firmament of heaven on the second day before dry land and plants appear on the third day. In Talmud Bavli Chagigah 12a–12b, Beit Hillel argues that the earth was created before the heavens, and Reish Lakish enumerates seven distinct firmaments by name, providing the rabbinic cosmology echoed in 41:9–12.

[11] Then He mounted (upward) to the sky, while it was (still) smoke, and said to it and to the earth, “Come, both of you, willingly or unwillingly!” They both said, “We come willingly.” [12] He finished them (as) seven heavens in two days, and inspired each heaven (with) its affair. sources.en: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel dispute the order of Creation, as the Sages taught: Beit Shammai say: The heavens were created first and afterward the earth was created, as it is stated: “In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth” (Genesis 1:1), which indicates that heaven came first. And Beit Hillel say: The earth was created first, and heaven after it, as it is stated: “On the day that the Lord God made earth and heaven” (Genesis 2:4).

cards.title: The Wives of Noah and Lot Betraying Their Righteous Husbands
cards.note: Surah 66:10 presents the wives of Noah and Lot as disbelievers who betrayed their righteous husbands, matching Midrash Bereishit Rabbah 51:5 where Lot's wife betrays the angelic guests to the Sodomites by asking neighbors for salt.

discussion.view: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir explain that the betrayal in 66:10 was in religion rather than marital chastity: Noah's wife called her husband mad and informed on believers, while Lot's wife signaled the presence of handsome guests to the people of Sodom.
discussion.reply: Genesis 19:26 states that Lot's wife looked back and became a pillar of salt without mentioning any plot against the guests. Midrash Bereishit Rabbah 51:5 supplies the narrative of betrayal, recording that she went to her neighbors asking for salt so the townsmen of Sodom would learn that guests were staying in Lot's house.

cards.quranEn: God has struck a parable for those who disbelieve: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot. They were under two of Our righteous servants, but they both betrayed them. Neither of them was of any use at all to either of them against God, when it was said, ‘Enter the Fire, both of you, with the ones who enter!’
quranHighlights: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot
They were under two of Our righteous servants, but they both betrayed them.

sources.title: Midrash Bereishit Rabbah (Genesis Rabbah)
sources.ref: Bereishit Rabbah 51:5 (Lot's Wife Betraying the Guests by Asking Neighbors for Salt)
sources.en: “His wife looked behind him, [and she became a pillar of salt]” – Rabbi Yitzḥak said: This was because she sinned with salt on that night that the angels came to Lot. What did she do? She went to all her neighbors and said to them: ‘Give me salt, as we have guests,’ and her intention was that the residents of the city should become aware of them. That is why “she became a pillar of salt.”
highlights: sinned with salt on that night that the angels came to Lot

cards.title: Noah Rebuking His Generation and Mocked by the Chiefs Before the Flood
cards.note: Surah 11:25–35 expands the Flood narrative into a public debate where Noah warns his people and the chiefs mock him and challenge him to bring the punishment, matching Talmud Bavli Sanhedrin 108b on Noah's rejected warnings.

discussion.view: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir view the extended dialogue between Noah and the chiefs of his people in 11:25–35 as a prophetic history revealed to comfort Muhammad against similar rejection by the Quraysh leadership in Mecca.
discussion.reply: In Genesis 6–7, Noah receives God's command and builds the ark in silence without addressing a single word of rebuke to his contemporaries. Talmud Bavli Sanhedrin 108b supplies the preaching and mockery scene, portraying Noah rebuking his generation with words harsh as torches while they deride him and challenge his warning of a flood.

cards.quranEn: [25] Certainly We sent Noah to his people: ‘I am a clear warner for you. [26] Do not serve (anyone) but God! Surely I fear for you the punishment of a painful Day.’ [27] The assembly of those who disbelieved of his people said, ‘We do not see you as (anything) but a human being like us, and we do not see following you (any) but the worst (and) most gullible of us. We do not see in you any superiority over us. No! We think you are liars.’ [28] He said, ‘My people! Do you see? If I (stand) on a clear sign from my Lord, and He has given me mercy from Himself, but it has been obscured for you, shall we compel you (to accept) it when you are unwilling? [29] My people! I do not ask you for any money for it. My reward (depends) only on God. I am not going to drive away those who believe. Surely they are going to meet their Lord, but I see that you are an ignorant people. [30] My people! Who would help me against God if I drove them away? Will you not take heed? [31] I do not say to you, “I possess the storehouses of God,” nor do I know the unseen. And I do not say, “I am an angel,” nor do I say to those your eyes look down on, “God will not give them any good.” God knows what is in them. Surely then I would indeed be one of the evildoers.’ [32] They said, ‘Noah! You have disputed with us, and disputed (too) much with us. Bring us what you promise us, if you are one of the truthful.’ [33] He said, ‘Only God will bring it to you, if He (so) pleases, and you will not escape. [34] My advice will not benefit you – (even) if I wish to advise you – if God wishes to make you err. He is your Lord, and to Him you will be returned.’ [35] Or do they say, ‘He has forged it’? Say: ‘If I have forged it, my sin is on me, but I am free of the sins you commit.’
quranHighlights: Certainly We sent Noah to his people: ‘I am a clear warner for you.
‘Noah! You have disputed with us, and disputed (too) much with us. Bring us what you promise us, if you are one of the truthful.’

sources.title: Talmud Bavli, Sanhedrin 108b

sources.en: This teaches that Noah the righteous would rebuke the people of his generation, and he said to them statements that are harsh as torches [kelapidim], and they would treat him with contempt. They said to him: Old man, why are you building this ark? Noah said to them: The Holy One, Blessed be He, is bringing a flood upon you. They said to him: A flood of what?

sources.orig: דָּרֵשׁ רָבָא: מַאי דִּכְתִיב ״לַפִּיד בּוּז לְעַשְׁתּוּת שַׁאֲנָן נָכוֹן לְמוֹעֲדֵי רָגֶל״? מְלַמֵּד שֶׁהָיָה נֹחַ הַצַּדִּיק מוֹכִיחַ אוֹתָם, וְאָמַר לָהֶם דְּבָרִים שֶׁהֵם קָשִׁים כְּלַפִּידִים, וְהָיוּ בּוֹזִים אוֹתוֹ. אָמְרוּ לוֹ: זָקֵן, תֵּיבָה זוֹ לָמָּה? אָמַר לָהֶם: הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מֵבִיא עֲלֵיכֶם אֶת הַמַּבּוּל. אָמְרוּ: מַבּוּל שֶׁל מָה?

cards.quranAr: وَلَقَدۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَا نُوحًا إِلَىٰ قَوۡمِهِۦٓ إِنِّي لَكُمۡ نَذِيرٞ مُّبِينٌ ﴿25﴾ أَن لَّا تَعۡبُدُوٓاْ إِلَّا ٱللَّهَۖ إِنِّيٓ أَخَافُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ عَذَابَ يَوۡمٍ أَلِيمٖ ﴿26﴾ فَقَالَ ٱلۡمَلَأُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِن قَوۡمِهِۦ مَا نَرَىٰكَ إِلَّا بَشَرٗا مِّثۡلَنَا وَمَا نَرَىٰكَ ٱتَّبَعَكَ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ هُمۡ أَرَاذِلُنَا بَادِيَ ٱلرَّأۡيِ وَمَا نَرَىٰ لَكُمۡ عَلَيۡنَا مِن فَضۡلِۭ بَلۡ نَظُنُّكُمۡ كَٰذِبِينَ ﴿27﴾ قَالَ يَٰقَوۡمِ أَرَءَيۡتُمۡ إِن كُنتُ عَلَىٰ بَيِّنَةٖ مِّن رَّبِّي وَءَاتَىٰنِي رَحۡمَةٗ مِّنۡ عِندِهِۦ فَعُمِّيَتۡ عَلَيۡكُمۡ أَنُلۡزِمُكُمُوهَا وَأَنتُمۡ لَهَا كَٰرِهُونَ ﴿28﴾ وَيَٰقَوۡمِ لَآ أَسۡـَٔلُكُمۡ عَلَيۡهِ مَالًاۖ إِنۡ أَجۡرِيَ إِلَّا عَلَى ٱللَّهِۚ وَمَآ أَنَا۠ بِطَارِدِ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْۚ إِنَّهُم مُّلَٰقُواْ رَبِّهِمۡ وَلَٰكِنِّيٓ أَرَىٰكُمۡ قَوۡمٗا تَجۡهَلُونَ ﴿29﴾ وَيَٰقَوۡمِ مَن يَنصُرُنِي مِنَ ٱللَّهِ إِن طَرَدتُّهُمۡۚ أَفَلَا تَذَكَّرُونَ ﴿30﴾ وَلَآ أَقُولُ لَكُمۡ عِندِي خَزَآئِنُ ٱللَّهِ وَلَآ أَعۡلَمُ ٱلۡغَيۡبَ وَلَآ أَقُولُ إِنِّي مَلَكٞ وَلَآ أَقُولُ لِلَّذِينَ تَزۡدَرِيٓ أَعۡيُنُكُمۡ لَن يُؤۡتِيَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ خَيۡرًاۖ ٱللَّهُ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَا فِيٓ أَنفُسِهِمۡ إِنِّيٓ إِذٗا لَّمِنَ ٱلظَّـٰلِمِينَ ﴿31﴾ قَالُواْ يَٰنُوحُ قَدۡ جَٰدَلۡتَنَا فَأَكۡثَرۡتَ جِدَٰلَنَا فَأۡتِنَا بِمَا تَعِدُنَآ إِن كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلصَّـٰدِقِينَ ﴿32﴾ قَالَ إِنَّمَا يَأۡتِيكُم بِهِ ٱللَّهُ إِن شَآءَ وَمَآ أَنتُم بِمُعۡجِزِينَ ﴿33﴾ وَلَا يَنفَعُكُمۡ نُصۡحِيٓ إِنۡ أَرَدتُّ أَنۡ أَنصَحَ لَكُمۡ إِن كَانَ ٱللَّهُ يُرِيدُ أَن يُغۡوِيَكُمۡۚ هُوَ رَبُّكُمۡ وَإِلَيۡهِ تُرۡجَعُونَ ﴿34﴾ أَمۡ يَقُولُونَ ٱفۡتَرَىٰهُۖ قُلۡ إِنِ ٱفۡتَرَيۡتُهُۥ فَعَلَيَّ إِجۡرَامِي وَأَنَا۠ بَرِيٓءٞ مِّمَّا تُجۡرِمُونَ ﴿35﴾

cards.title: First Human from Clay, Progeny from Fluid, and Threefold Endowment
cards.note: Surah 32:7–9 distinguishes creating the first human from clay, his progeny from 'despicable water' (ma' mahin), and God breathing His spirit to grant hearing, sight, and hearts, matching Pirkei Avot 3:1 ('putrid drop') and Talmud Niddah 31a.

discussion.view: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir explain that 32:7–9 separates Adam's original formation from clay from the reproduction of his descendants through seminal fluid, followed by the ensoulment of the fetus and the gift of sensory faculties.
discussion.reply: Genesis 2:7 describes Adam's formation from dust and the breath of life, while Mishnah Pirkei Avot 3:1 coins the moral maxim that every human comes from a 'putrid drop' (tippah seruchah), rendered in Arabic as ma' mahin. Talmud Bavli Niddah 31a further assigns spirit, sight of the eye, hearing of the ear, and understanding of the heart specifically to God's contribution.

cards.quranEn: [7] who made well everything He created. He brought about the creation of the human from clay, [8] then He made his progeny from an extract of despicable water, [9] then He fashioned him and breathed into him some of His spirit, and made for you hearing and sight and hearts. Little thanks you show!
quranHighlights: He brought about the creation of the human from clay
then He made his progeny from an extract of despicable water
breathed into him some of His spirit, and made for you hearing and sight and hearts

sources.title: Mishnah Pirkei Avot
sources.en: From where do you come? From a putrid drop. Where are you going? To a place of dust, of worm and of maggot. Before whom you are destined to give an account and reckoning? Before the King of the kings of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He.
highlights: From where do you come? From a putrid drop.
To a place of dust, of worm and of maggot.
sources.orig: עֲקַבְיָא בֶן מַהֲלַלְאֵל אוֹמֵר, הִסְתַּכֵּל בִּשְׁלשָׁה דְבָרִים וְאִי אַתָּה בָא לִידֵי עֲבֵרָה. דַּע מֵאַיִן בָּאתָ, וּלְאָן אַתָּה הוֹלֵךְ, וְלִפְנֵי מִי אַתָּה עָתִיד לִתֵּן דִּין וְחֶשְׁבּוֹן. מֵאַיִן בָּאתָ, מִטִּפָּה סְרוּחָה, וּלְאָן אַתָּה הוֹלֵךְ, לִמְקוֹם עָפָר רִמָּה וְתוֹלֵעָה. וְלִפְנֵי מִי אַתָּה עָתִיד לִתֵּן דִּין וְחֶשְׁבּוֹן, לִפְנֵי מֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:

sources.title: Talmud Bavli, Tractate Niddah
sources.en: The Sages taught: There are three partners in the creation of a person: The Holy One, Blessed be He, and his father, and his mother. His father emits the white seed, from which the following body parts are formed: The bones, the sinews, the nails, the brain that is in its head, and the white of the eye. His mother emits red seed, from which are formed the skin, the flesh, the hair, and the black of the eye. And the Holy One, Blessed be He, inserts into him a spirit, a soul, his countenance [ukelaster], eyesight, hearing of the ear, the capability of speech of the mouth, the capability of walking with the legs, understanding, and wisdom.
highlights: There are three partners in the creation of a person
And the Holy One, Blessed be He, inserts into him a spirit, a soul

cards.title: Surah 5 Review of Jesus' Clay Birds, Healings, and Sorcery Accusation
cards.note: In God's direct address to Jesus in 5:110, breathing life into a clay bird stands alongside speaking in the cradle and the Israelites calling his signs 'clear magic,' matching the Infancy Gospel of Thomas 2:2–4 and Talmud Sanhedrin 43a.

discussion.view: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir read 5:110 as God's covenantal reminder to Jesus enumerating the miracles granted to him by divine permission (bi-idhni) to distinguish prophetic signs from divine sonship.
discussion.reply: Unlike 3:49, where Jesus announces these signs to Israel, 5:110 frames them as God's retrospective address and adds the Israelites' charge that his signs were 'clear magic.' That passage unites the second-century Infancy Gospel of Thomas 2:2–4 (animating clay sparrows) with the rabbinic verdict in Talmud Sanhedrin 43a that Jesus practiced sorcery and led Israel astray.

And when I taught you the Book and the wisdom, and the Torah and the Gospel. cards.title: God Commanding the Furnace to Be Coolness and Peace for Abraham
cards.note: In Surah 21:68–70, the crowd cries 'Burn him and help your gods' and God commands the fire to be 'coolness and peace for Abraham,' following the midrashic reading of 'Ur of the Chaldeans' (Genesis 11:28) as a fiery furnace in Bereishit Rabbah 38:13.

discussion.view: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir narrate from Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid that Nimrod and his people built an enclosure of firewood, hurled Abraham into the blaze by catapult, and saw the flames rendered harmless by God's decree 'O fire, be coolness and peace.'
discussion.reply: In Genesis 11:28, 'Ur of the Chaldeans' (Hebrew Ur Kasdim, rendered in the Greek Septuagint as 'the country of the Chaldees') is the Mesopotamian city of Abraham's birth. Because the Hebrew noun ur also means 'fire' or 'flame,' Jewish exegetes in Bereishit Rabbah 38:13 read Ur Kasdim as 'the fiery furnace of the Chaldeans,' generating the narrative of Nimrod casting Abraham into the furnace echoed in 21:68–70.
